newsitem.title: GERMANY: German construction union, employers avert strike.
newsitem.headline: German construction union, employers avert strike.

text.p: Germany's troubled construction industry averted the threat of its first big strike since 1950 Friday when union representatives and employers agreed to a compromise deal.
The agreement came just five days before a deadline for a strike vote that could have plunged the sector even deeper into recession.

The new deal offers better sick pay arrangements than an earlier proposal that the union had rejected Monday, but employers still expect a reduction in labour costs via a below-inflation 1.3 percent pay raise and falls in sick pay and holiday bonus entitlements.
The deal covers 1.3 million workers in western Germany, of whom about 400,000 are unemployed.
The two sides failed to agree on pay for 380,000 construction workers in eastern Germany and said they would resume talks at a later date.
